author: Eluaria
subject: Re: New Mage presenting
content_md:
Hello there, welcome to Mage ^^
Frost does decent damage, but it is incredibly reliant on RNG Flash Freeze Procs due to Frostbite, which means you may end up in fights where you legitimately not cast a single Icicle, Frost's major damage spell, since you don't get a single proc.

Arcane is, by a large Margin, the strongest spec, Frost has (sadly) nowhere close to the ability to do damage as Arcane does. You want Cast Speed for this spec more than Crit or Pure Spell Power, but most of the good pieces that give Haste come from Molten Core. There are outliers from some dungeon quests, and Stormwind Vault though.

The biggest issue is, that Frost (and Fire) don't actually have any form of Tiersets that make a difference for them. Whereas Arcane actually does something, Frost and Fire are stuck with Boni such as "Do a bit less Threat" or "Increase the radius of Flamestrike and Blizzard by 15%".
That said, if you want to invest the time and gold into it, Frost benefits a lot from our Second Tier Dungeon Set. A 5% chance to trigger freeze whenever you take damage, which in turn causes Flash Freeze to proc.
It's kinda sad that Arcane is so much stronger than Frost, since Frost honestly feels more fun than Arcane does.

Fire is sadly not viable until after Blackwing Lair, since several bosses in both Molten Core and BWL are Fire immune, a relic of a time when that didn't make sense, but still was done. It should do better than Frost once it can actually do damage though.

author: Kibuum
subject: Arcane Mage in 1.17.2
content_md:
(Only talking about group PvE)

Arcane will lose Brilliance and therefore its role as a support caster, and on the other hand gain improved dmg capabilities, esp. Arcane Rupture and the synergy between Accelerated Arcana and Arcane Power.
Time will tell if this makes Arcane viable, utterly useless or OPTM, but since this forum lacks a discussion about the new skills and possible builds, I wanted to start it:

What to pair Arcane with? Fire, Frost, or a mix of both?
[My take atm.](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?points=VAAoLIAaBKAoBAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAQYDTBDQAAAAAAAA%3D)

Thoughts on Arcane Instability? Will it proc of every hit of Arcane Missiles [AM] like Arcane Concentration?
Is it worth the added risk combined with Arcane Power?

And gear! Will cast speed become more important than crit? What could be new BIS items? [Chromie's Broken Pocket Watch looks insane.](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61564)

Also: Will Rupture buff all AM-projectiles of a single cast, even if it runs out during the channeling? If so, then bringing AM channeling down to under 4,5 seconds would increase dmg of two full AM-casts. That would be possible with 12% casting speed increase, which is rather doable with Accelerated Arcana providing the first 6%.

And Presence of Mind: What is it for?

author: Schoop123
subject: Feedback after leveling 1-60 as Arcane in 1.17.2
content_md:
After reading the class changes when they first dropped a few weeks ago, I decided to level all the way to 60 with the Arcane changes to see how they feel, here's my feedback from that journey. It's pretty long, so if you decide to read it, thanks in advance!

 1. **The Good**:
First of all, I'm a huge fan of the ideas behind the changes, with the focus on mana management and the effectively 3 different crit effects with Arcane Instability and Resonance Cascade, it makes it feel like the power is hard to control and fits Arcane perfectly in my opinion.

I also really like the idea of the Accelerated Arcana talent, reducing CDs of all Arcane spells based on casting speed gives a great new way of using stats, such as using Arcane Power to reduce the CD of Blink for movement (though not much else while leveling, more on that later). It also made me look everywhere I could to find more casting speed, something I'm a big fan of, even if there aren't that many sources while leveling.

There's also a ton of talents that you want, which means there's a lot of different ways you could build and still play "correctly", which is cool.

 2. **The Bad**:
 2.1. **Arcane Power**
The obvious one here for me is Arcane Power - I think the idea behind it is cool, and I think it's clear that the idea is to make even fully raid geared Mages care about mana, but this way of doing it makes it so that leveling Mages will basically never want to use it at all. For example, if you want more power to kill an elite, you'll instead just go oom and die because of it. If you want to use it to kill general mobs faster you'll just have to drink more, effectively wasting time rather than the opposite. The only use I've found for it is to use it to cast teleport faster, and to reduce the CD of Blink.

It also seems like it's contrary to the design of the tree in general - while the tree as a whole seems to revolve around mana management, Arcane Power punishes you for having a lot of Intellect (*by draining more of your mana*) and drastically reducing the value of your Spirit, and making your own ways of restoring mana (*Evocation and Mana Gem*) useless for the duration (*note: currently only Evocation and your Spirit mana regen is affected, I'm not sure if this is intended*). I feel like it'd fit the tree better if you wanted to use all of your tricks during Arcane Power to not die.

Also, it currently gives 25% casting speed rather than 35% as stated in the tooltip. Not sure if this is a bug.

 2.2. **Burst**
The unfortunate side effect of having 3 different forms of crit is that when all of them happen at once the amount of damage you can do is absolutely crazy. Arcane Rupture hits pretty hard on its own, but with Resonance Cascade being a potential 1.75x damage increase, Arcane Potency making crits 2x damage increase, and Arcane Instability being a potential 1.25x damage increase, you can sometimes hit (*1.75*2*1.25=*) **4.375** times harder than a normal cast, which is pretty problematic in PvP I feel.

 2.3. **Suggestions**
If the functionality of making geared Mages care about mana is important to maintain, you could change **Arcane Power** to drain some of your max mana for each spell hit (*1% for each hit? including Cascades*), remove the reduced mana gains, and give an amount of **base** mana regen per second (*something like 5% per second, which is 60/s at level 60*). This makes it so that the spell is useful at all levels of content, makes you care about mana somewhat even in late endgame, and becomes useful while leveling in a different way from while raiding.

As for **burst**, I think the easiest solution is to make Arcane Rupture do a lot less damage and compensate by making Arcane Missiles better (*more on this later*). It won't matter that a crit can do 4.375x damage if your hits in general are fairly weak but numerous.

 3. **The Awkward**:
This section isn't really anything I can say is objective, it's just what I personally feel could be improved. First of all:

 3.1. **Intellect bad?**
While obviously yes, Vanilla class design in general doesn't really make any spec want to stack Intellect, I've always felt like if any spec should want it, it would be Arcane. With the current spec design, especially with Arcane Power draining a % of your max mana, Intellect feels *worse* for Arcane than for other casters. Until you can start stacking spelldamage and casting speed, it feels like Spirit is your main stat. Spirit being good isn't a bad thing, but I feel like Intellect should also be strong.

 3.2. **No great talents in the other trees**
While this definitely isn't a necessary thing to improve, I think it'd be great to pay homage to the roots of Arcane being a support tree to the other specs (*PoM Pyro, Arcane Frost*), by giving a reason to use spells from the other trees occasionally.

 3.3. **Arcane Rupture buff weirdness**
The fact that this buff lasts for 8 seconds and doesn't buff a cast that's started right before it ends but does increase the mana cost is awkward, it feels like you're punished for casting a second Arcane Missiles in the window unless you have enough cast speed to make a cast take 4 seconds.

 3.4. **Arcane Missiles still feel bad, especially early**
The spec is currently very reliant on either Arcane Rupture or the later talents for Arcane Missiles to feel better than the other main casts even with Arcane talents. Even with them though, the cast is just a little too sluggish to feel really good. I imagine this'd be fixed somewhat with raiding gear.

 3.5. **Suggestions**
To improve Intellect as a stat, I'd add an effect to a deep talent to do one or both of the following: 50% of your Intellect is added as Spirit, 20% of your Intellect is added as Spell Damage. The former at least makes Intellect relevant for leveling, while the latter gives some base Spell Damage that feels like it would be appropriate for Arcane. Intellect still wouldn't be the main stat for raiding, and I think that's fine.

To make other trees more relevant for offtalents, I'd add an effect that makes it so that every hit (*ie every hit of Arcane Explosion, every wave of Arcane Missiles, and every proc of Cascade and Instability*) of an Arcane spell increases the crit chance of your next Fire/Frost spell by 2%, stacking up to 50. I don't even know if this is possible with the Vanilla client, but I feel it'd do a lot to spice up the rotation without making stuff like PoM Pyro OP.

Though I'd like to see Arcane Rupture fully buffing any cast that was started while the buff was active regardless.

I think the ideas overall for the spec are great, and the changes have managed to make Arcane feel like a proper spec for sure which is impressive considering how little there was to begin with. The added stuff feels mostly appropriate for Vanilla while still being fun to use. If anyone read this far, thanks for reading!
content_html:
After reading the class changes when they first dropped a few weeks ago, I decided to level all the way to 60 with the Arcane changes to see how they feel, here's my feedback from that journey. It's pretty long, so if you decide to read it, thanks in advance!

1. The Good:
First of all, I'm a huge fan of the ideas behind the changes, with the focus on mana management and the effectively 3 different crit effects with Arcane Instability and Resonance Cascade, it makes it feel like the power is hard to control and fits Arcane perfectly in my opinion.

I also really like the idea of the Accelerated Arcana talent, reducing CDs of all Arcane spells based on casting speed gives a great new way of using stats, such as using Arcane Power to reduce the CD of Blink for movement (though not much else while leveling, more on that later). It also made me look everywhere I could to find more casting speed, something I'm a big fan of, even if there aren't that many sources while leveling.

There's also a ton of talents that you want, which means there's a lot of different ways you could build and still play "correctly", which is cool.

2. The Bad:
2.1. Arcane Power
The obvious one here for me is Arcane Power - I think the idea behind it is cool, and I think it's clear that the idea is to make even fully raid geared Mages care about mana, but this way of doing it makes it so that leveling Mages will basically never want to use it at all. For example, if you want more power to kill an elite, you'll instead just go oom and die because of it. If you want to use it to kill general mobs faster you'll just have to drink more, effectively wasting time rather than the opposite. The only use I've found for it is to use it to cast teleport faster, and to reduce the CD of Blink.

It also seems like it's contrary to the design of the tree in general - while the tree as a whole seems to revolve around mana management, Arcane Power punishes you for having a lot of Intellect (by draining more of your mana) and drastically reducing the value of your Spirit, and making your own ways of restoring mana (Evocation and Mana Gem) useless for the duration (note: currently only Evocation and your Spirit mana regen is affected, I'm not sure if this is intended). I feel like it'd fit the tree better if you wanted to use all of your tricks during Arcane Power to not die.

Also, it currently gives 25% casting speed rather than 35% as stated in the tooltip. Not sure if this is a bug.

2.2. Burst
The unfortunate side effect of having 3 different forms of crit is that when all of them happen at once the amount of damage you can do is absolutely crazy. Arcane Rupture hits pretty hard on its own, but with Resonance Cascade being a potential 1.75x damage increase, Arcane Potency making crits 2x damage increase, and Arcane Instability being a potential 1.25x damage increase, you can sometimes hit (1.75*2*1.25=) 4.375 times harder than a normal cast, which is pretty problematic in PvP I feel.

2.3. Suggestions
If the functionality of making geared Mages care about mana is important to maintain, you could change Arcane Power to drain some of your max mana for each spell hit (1% for each hit? including Cascades), remove the reduced mana gains, and give an amount of base mana regen per second (something like 5% per second, which is 60/s at level 60). This makes it so that the spell is useful at all levels of content, makes you care about mana somewhat even in late endgame, and becomes useful while leveling in a different way from while raiding.

As for burst, I think the easiest solution is to make Arcane Rupture do a lot less damage and compensate by making Arcane Missiles better (more on this later). It won't matter that a crit can do 4.375x damage if your hits in general are fairly weak but numerous.

3. The Awkward:
This section isn't really anything I can say is objective, it's just what I personally feel could be improved. First of all:

3.1. Intellect bad?
While obviously yes, Vanilla class design in general doesn't really make any spec want to stack Intellect, I've always felt like if any spec should want it, it would be Arcane. With the current spec design, especially with Arcane Power draining a % of your max mana, Intellect feels worse for Arcane than for other casters. Until you can start stacking spelldamage and casting speed, it feels like Spirit is your main stat. Spirit being good isn't a bad thing, but I feel like Intellect should also be strong.

3.2. No great talents in the other trees
While this definitely isn't a necessary thing to improve, I think it'd be great to pay homage to the roots of Arcane being a support tree to the other specs (PoM Pyro, Arcane Frost), by giving a reason to use spells from the other trees occasionally.

3.3. Arcane Rupture buff weirdness
The fact that this buff lasts for 8 seconds and doesn't buff a cast that's started right before it ends but does increase the mana cost is awkward, it feels like you're punished for casting a second Arcane Missiles in the window unless you have enough cast speed to make a cast take 4 seconds.

3.4. Arcane Missiles still feel bad, especially early
The spec is currently very reliant on either Arcane Rupture or the later talents for Arcane Missiles to feel better than the other main casts even with Arcane talents. Even with them though, the cast is just a little too sluggish to feel really good. I imagine this'd be fixed somewhat with raiding gear.

3.5. Suggestions
To improve Intellect as a stat, I'd add an effect to a deep talent to do one or both of the following: 50% of your Intellect is added as Spirit, 20% of your Intellect is added as Spell Damage. The former at least makes Intellect relevant for leveling, while the latter gives some base Spell Damage that feels like it would be appropriate for Arcane. Intellect still wouldn't be the main stat for raiding, and I think that's fine.

To make other trees more relevant for offtalents, I'd add an effect that makes it so that every hit (ie every hit of Arcane Explosion, every wave of Arcane Missiles, and every proc of Cascade and Instability) of an Arcane spell increases the crit chance of your next Fire/Frost spell by 2%, stacking up to 50. I don't even know if this is possible with the Vanilla client, but I feel it'd do a lot to spice up the rotation without making stuff like PoM Pyro OP.

To both improve Missiles and to reduce the awkwardness of the Arcane Rupture buff, I'd reduce the time between each wave to 0.8 sec, 4 sec total for max ranks (and reduce the scaling so it doesn't outscale Frostbolt/Fireball). Though I'd like to see Arcane Rupture fully buffing any cast that was started while the buff was active regardless.

4. Final notes
I think the ideas overall for the spec are great, and the changes have managed to make Arcane feel like a proper spec for sure which is impressive considering how little there was to begin with. The added stuff feels mostly appropriate for Vanilla while still being fun to use. While I've got a fair few suggestions in this post, I don't at all think all of them are necessary for Arcane to feel great, but rather they're just everything I've thought would improve the complete feeling of it.

If anyone read this far, thanks for reading!

This summarizes pretty much my feelings about Arcane - but I will extend on something I think it's worth mentioning as I see you mentioned the lack of options in other talents for pure Arcane mages and the lack of options to use Arcane tree as a support tree for other specs.

Deep Arcane tree needs something for other specs. It used to have AP but now most of the times people won't even go there even for Presence of Mind. This change killed Arcane + Fire/Frost specs.

Making **Arcane Potency** (+100% crit damage, due to how this works it would add 50% crit damage to fire and 50% to frost) **work on all schools and moving it down a tier** would allow those specs back.

By moving it down a tier it would open for many options in Fire/Frost trees where players would need to choose between a pool of relevant talents and take the most important for them. Frost would get much bigger crits at the cost of the new Flash Freeze and Fire would be able to get bigger Ignites/Crits at the cost of base damage/crit.

And because of how Arcane tree for pure Arcane mages is so full, Arcane Mages wouldn't suffer from this change as they already want to put all talent points there anyway.

Arcane rupture's 8 sec window is something to be reconsidered. It just doesn't make sense to spend the extra mana on the second cast if you don't even get the added damage. It would be nice if the damage buff was applied to the whole duration if the mana cost was raised on the spell.

My suggestion here would be to make Arcane Rupture not to consume mana instead of refounding it, and Clearcasting not to trigger when Temporal Convergence is in effect on Arcane Rupture cast.

My suggestion here would be to make Arcane Rupture not to consume mana instead of refounding it, and Clearcasting not to trigger when Temporal Convergence is in effect on Arcane Rupture cast.

author: Turboman
subject: Re: Blink is broke in the air?
content_md:
For this feature to work flawlessly you need a perfect surface beneath you (no collisions, not too curvy), if you appeared to be higher after blink that means that your "hit" some object on the ground in front of you or a surface curve.
Oh and also it works on certain height in my experience. If you press blink to soon, then you're get put higher with fall speed reset.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Blink is broke in the air?

If you blink from more than 20 meters in height, you blink in place as the game finds no spot to place you. It looks like it teleports you up due to input delay.

Its one of those lessons you just need to learn. Blink when you are low. Not high up

author: Forumdweller
subject: Remember when mages had..
content_md:
3 spell schools that each served a different purpose?

Frost was primarily for CC'ing (well frost also did insane damage but lets ignore that)
Fire was primarily for doing dps
Arcane was primarily for utility, counterspell, blink, poly, spammable burst aoe and mana shield

now every spell school does insane damage so you kick one school and u start getting blasted by another. seems like a completely fair gameplay mechanic to basically be immune to kicks now

these are the sort of things u need to think about when making class changes.

author: Mitzter
subject: Re: Remember when mages had..
content_md:
Its no different than actual vanilla.
Kick a mage's frostbolt? They do scorch, fireblast (or blastwave if elementalist spec), poly, missiles, explosion
Kick a mage's fireball or scorch? They do cone of cold, frost nova, poly, arcane missiles, explosion.
Kick a mage's missiles? Lel block.

Them having access to throw out a different dmging spell isn't anything new, its why blanket silence exists. Against a mage the rule of thumb was silencing arcane as top priority if blink isnt on CD and he is safe to poly properly, otherwise silence his mainspec school. Silencing elementalist is trickier, but seeing as how there are no mages playing that particular hybrid spec on this server, its a nonissue.

Whats the difference here? That mages just do more dmg? Everyone else does.

Wheres the difference with interrupting a balance druid? Interrupt starfire and he does wrath. Interrupt wrath and he turborams his moonfire key.

Wheres the difference with interrupting a warlock? Interrupt his fear and he does immolate or searing pain. Interrupt searing pain and he does fear, coil, sbolt or w/e.

author: Atolius
subject: Battlemage/Spellsword/Spellblade might be possible (while leveling)
content_md:
Hi Turtles,

I'm leveling right now as an instant-cast melee mage, and it seems quite viable so far. I don't expect it will scale well, but am level 26 and having a blast. Its damage is competitive and survivability is off the charts with Mana Shield and Counterspell even with low stamina gear. Throw in the Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer buff for even more fun and heavy crits. It seems to outperform ranged Arcane in overall damage and lasting power with this buff.

Yes, I know Shamans exist. This is fully for RP flavor and those who are willing to experiment or wish to try out a melee spellcaster with an Alliance race.

The trick is to have the right speed of staff and wand, and to weave them appropriately with the instant cast spells. Right now, I have Staff of the Friar ([https://www.wowhead.com/classic/item=34 ... -the-friar](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/item=3415/staff-of-the-friar)) and Thunderwood (<https://www.wowhead.com/classic/item=13062/thunderwood>).

The staff speed is 2.6 and wand speed is 1.9. Wands on Turtle WoW don't reset swing timers. Hitting melee and then wand once the hit animation activates gets me to be able to weave one wand cast in between each weapon swing within the swing timer. It might extend it a very little bit, something like 0.1 seconds, but works well together.

Dramatically lower or higher weapon speeds than this may either not work well with the wand or be too fast to weave wands with the 1.5 second default GCD, so I'd aim for as close to those two speeds for staves and wands as possible. Swords and off-hand with similar speeds is also likely to work, though not as heavy in melee.

My gear prioritizes the stats as follows: Attack Power, Agility, Spirit, Intellect, Stamina, and everything else. "of the Wolf" (AGI/SPI), "of the Falcon" (AGI/INT), "of Agility", "of the Owl" (INT/SPI), and "of the Monkey" (AGI/STAM) gear names are sought after in that order. Agility increases wand and possibly also melee crit once you have enough weapon skill. Amber Rings give +6 AP and you can acquire them early and keep them for a long time.

Always, always have your weapon and defense skills at highest levels. You will notice a big change if starting out versus having these full.

My current rotation is this:

Mana Shield
Arcane Rupture
Wand once
Melee
 - Once the staff hits, Fire Blast
 - Wand once (this wand + FB will reset or extend the swing timer, I've noticed)
Melee
Wand once
Melee
 - By this time, mp5 will be active and FB will be off cooldown. Use FB or melee more for mana as desired.
Wand
When Clearcasting procs, use missiles.
Use Arcane Explosion and Cone of Cold anytime FB is on cooldown, in a separate swing timer interval, if you have the mana.

Etc.

With Arcane Meditation, regeneration is tripled below 30% mana. This is important to get even more casts of Arcane Explosion off. Lowest rank AE can regen fully under these conditions and proc Clearcasting.

Talents now:
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?poi ... AAAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?points=AoQoJIQCAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=)

Variants:

Arcane Battlemage
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?poi ... AAAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?points=AoToLIQbZKAoAAAoQYAIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=)

Fire Battlemage
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?poi ... AAAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?points=AoToIAADAAAAAAAooYQIYDLAAoBAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=)

Frost Battlemage
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?poi ... DoBDAABAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?points=AoToIAADAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAFAbQpADoBDAABAA=)

Tri-spec Battlemage (get Shatter first)
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?poi ... AoAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/mage?points=AoQoIAAAAAAAAAAooQQIADAAAAAAFAbQJAAoAAAAAAA=)

I basically boost damage for instants and skip the resistance talents except for Magic Absorption because Arcane Surge at level 32 will be a powerful DPS boost for all variants, potentially.

Lastly, anytime Seal of Wisdom is on an enemy, you will regenerate a LOT of mana and can use far more instant casts. Try it out on a training dummy when a Paladin is using it, and unless you're using Cone of Cold a lot, Fire Blast and Arcane Explosion at highest ranks can be used perpetually. Below 30% mana with Seal of Wisdom on the enemy and Arcane Meditation, it doesn't matter what instant spell you cast. You can do it forever with the rotation.

I'm not saying this build is the best, but it's something to try out for fun and seems very good so far. Let me know your experiences with it and if anyone can post any DPS numbers/survivability impressions. This method also requires very little to any drinking and eating downtime if you time the spells well with mp5 regen intervals.

The last point I'll say is if they could make a baseline mage ability like the one below, it could probably work.

Battlemage Aura:

 - Decreases casting/channeling range to 3 or 5 yards while in combat (targets which then move out of this range could still be hit by that spellcast)
 - Increases melee attack power by a portion of INT or even AGI

A long CD for the aura could help force one playstyle or the other in cases where blending range with melee breaks balance.

Not sure what to do about the melee miss chance and glancing blows vs. the same and higher levels...

subject: Yet another Battlemage spec idea
content_md:
Hello all,

I love battlemages and I just couldn't help myself from creating a subspec for them. Plus, they're an established part of the lore along with High Elves and not represented at all as being available to players in retail, which is a shame.

Here's a failed implementation using wand weaving which loses to scaling at around level 30, but is fun before then:

[viewtopic.php?t=19612](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=19612)

Below, I detail 3 talents in the Arcane tree which can be made to create a hopefully satisfying Battlemage experience while not stepping on the toes of other specs and classes due to imbalance. Let me know your thoughts while paying attention to the magical damage reductions that are outlined. Would this scale well? What needs to be changed?

If Turtle WoW ever adds additional classes or subspecs, and this is implemented, any ridicule now would be worth it.

Dragon Age: Origins fans may recognize the flavor of some of these abilities. This was my favorite implementation of battlemage in games, so I used it loosely as a model here.

NEW ARCANE TALENTS FOR BATTLEMAGES:

[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... nc8yPO&c=0](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator/custom?t0=ki0KtKJpvi&t1=J21Cma0V44&t2=R4M5nc8yPO&c=0)

 1) Battlemage Training
Row 1 talent
 1 point

Channels magic inward to increase your physical ability at the expense of spell potency.

Replaces Strength and Agility with Intellect.
Can equip leather armor, mail armor, and shields.
Magical damage dealt decreased by 25% plus 2% per leather item, 3% per mail item, and 10% for a shield.
You can now parry and block attacks.

In addition, your melee attacks have a 5% chance to make your next Arcane Rupture, Fireball, or Frostbolt instant cast and cost half mana. This effect cannot occur more than once per minute.

 2) Magic Weapons
Row 2 talent
 1 point
Requires Battlemage Training

Grants access to the following four abilities:

Arcane (Fire, Frost) Weapon
Instant
 1% of base mana
Imbues your weapon with magic, causing 10% of weapon damage as additional Arcane (Fire, Frost) damage. This damage ignores reduction effects from Battlemage Training. Does not stack with other magic weapon imbues, but does stack with other weapon enhancements. Lasts 30 minutes.

Spellstrike
Instant, melee range
 10 second CD
 0.5% of base mana
Hits for 100% of weapon damage, plus 100% of weapon damage as spell damage, split between the nearest 4 enemies within 8 yards. The spell school chosen is determined by the active magic weapon imbue. Cannot be used without a magic weapon imbue. Can be used off global cooldown. This damage is not affected by Battlemage Training reduction effects and can proc Clearcasting.

 3) Arcane Warrior
Row 3 talent
 1 point
Requires Imbue Magic

Grants access to the following abilities:

Combat Magic
 3 second cast
 10% of base mana
Increases all weapon skills by 2, Spellstrike damage by 10%, and Arcane Weapon, Fire Weapon, and Frost Weapon damage by 50%. Cannot be used with Defensive Magic. Active until cancelled.

Defensive Magic
 3 second cast
 10% of base mana
Increases threat generated by 250% and reduces damage taken by 2%. Mana Shield now absorbs 1.33 damage per mana point, absorbs double the total amount of damage, and generates threat equal to the damage absorbed. Your Fire Blast now taunts an enemy to attack you if it is not currently attacking you. This effect ignores Fire immunity and has a 10 second cooldown. Cannot be used with Combat Magic. Active until cancelled.

Let's hear your thoughts.

author: Avalok
subject: Mage Arcane Talents & Spells Adjustments
content_md:
**HELLO!**

In this topic, I would like to suggest some adjustments on two talents in the Arcane Talent Tree,
and one Arcane Spell as well, for the Arcane Mages of Turtle-WoW! ---  happy_turtle_head

 1. ***Arcane Concentration*** (Talent)

I notice there has been added an "occurrence-in-time" mechanic on said talent. Just so you know, this mechanic didn't exist before. *What I would like to suggest is increasing the occurrence amount of the talent buff to twice (2), instead of just once (1), and also allow for the talent buff to be able to stack on the Mage for two (2) times as well.* You can also nerf the occurrence-in-time's duration to 10 or 12 seconds, instead of 8, if that would seem more fair.

The reason for this is because Arcane Missiles (AM) can actually proc the said talent multiple times in one channeling... Back then, when the talent, Arcane Concentration (AC), was not yet adjusted with an occurrence mechanic, the Mage can proc the said talent multiple times in one channeling of 'AM,' which seemed pretty silly, and kind of OP without the practicality included.

 2. ***Arcane Surge*** (Spell)

An important and subtle detail regarding this spell, Arcane Surge, is that it has an availability duration of what I believe to be four (4) seconds 'only,' after any other damaging spell hit of the Mage is partially or fully resisted by his target.

 *What I would like to suggest regarding this spell is to increase the duration of its availability to six (6) seconds, instead of just four (4) seconds.* It is because, sometimes, Arcane Surge (AS) will only trigger near the end of the channeling of Arcane Missiles (AM). By that time, it would have already been too late for me to be able cast 'AS' as I have already casted my next channel of 'AM.' After the duration of the channel, 'AS' would no longer be available.

 *Another suggestion I would like to give regarding this spell is to just remove its mana cost...* When using this spell, 'AS,' while having an 'AC' buff present on me would cause it to consume the latter, which is really just a bother... That 'AC' buff would have been much better off being consumed by a channel of Arcane Missiles.

 3. ***Temporal Convergence*** (Talent)

 *If it is possible, could you guys please adjust the talent, Temporal Convergence (TC), so that when the buff of said talent affects the Mage, it will not also consume an Arcane Concentration (AC) buff, if it is also present on him?* When an 'AC' buff and a 'TC' buff are both present on the Mage, both will be consumed after casting Arcane Rupture, which really feels like much of a waste to be honest.

Temporal Convergence is much like an Arcane Concentration buff, but it only affects one particular spell, which is the 'Arcane Rupture' spell from the Arcane Talent Tree. I personally do not like using Arcane Rupture, because I'm a bit too conscious with mana conservation. My rotation is simply just spamming Arcane Missiles, with the occasional Arcane Surge.

 *Maybe the said talent, 'TC,' could be adjusted to restore only half the mana it consumes instead, or some other mechanic that could go along well with it (nerfed if needed), so long as there are no 'AC' buffs consumed when it is active on the Mage along with 'TC' buff.* I hope that an adjustment could be implemented on this talent.

 ----------

That is all.   happy_turtle    Thank you for your time.

author: Eluaria
subject: Re: Mage Arcane Talents & Spells Adjustments
content_md:
Arcane Concentration is fine as it is post nerf. We mages do not struggle with Mana nearly as much as Mage Players love to make people believe. In Raids, as soon as a single Retribution Paladin puts the Mana on Spell Hit debuff on a target, your Mana Bar essentially just goes to full. We do not need additional Mana Resource Spares like a second Clear Casting buff.

Arcane Surge definitely has the availability as an issue, but that is in term with a lot of consistency issues, Turtle has introduced or has left untouched. It also really doesn't need to have its Mana cost removed either. Casting Surge or Missles to consume Clearcasting is a choice you make. It shouldn't be a braindead "Oh, I just cast Surge no matter what", unless you want to introduce even more power into an already powerful spec.

The same goes for Temporal Convergence. You have more than enough time to cast 3 Missles into a proc without the proc running out. Casting Arcane Blast should be a choice, not an auto click.

author: Guldred
subject: Arcane Surge and haste
content_md:
Hello,

I was wondering if it is intended or an oversight that Arcane Surge (its GCD) does not scale with haste (and you can't improve by talents like Fire Blast). The problem with this being that while the spell is great at low haste value, due to the lack of scaling with haste you dont use it in burst phases.

As far as theorycrafting goes, the threshold lies at about 30% which you reach with Mind Quickening Gem or Arcane Power or the Sphere of endless Gulch (given you are at about 10% haste without the proc of the Sphere).

So when we go into burst mode, one of our 3 skills just falls flat and gets kicked out of the rotation.

Thats unfortunate since it is great fun to go after those procs at the last possible second, even canceling missiles for them sometimes.

Best regards,

Guldred

author: Manletow
subject: Reworked Arcane & Frost (PVP Variant)
content_md:
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/A2kiBdg.png)

Blizz had deeply admirable concepts in regards to thematics and 'flavor' for Mage and its Trees -- these being very important in a fantasy Role Playing game.
...but overall they did quite poorly as there is a whole array of highly over/underpowered abilities and Talents.

Sadly, the T-WoW devs did not adequately address the mistakes of their forefathers...
AND went even further down a twisted path by adding ill-conceived, custom, Raid-brained DPS shlock.

> 'making Arcane Missiles viable in PVP' was HIGHLY commendable. they likely did this by accident however.

I reworked Arcane and made minor (but important) tweaks to Frost.
Yes, there will be (long overdue/well-deserved) nerfs im afraid.
This is to *primarily* improve the overall health/enjoyment of PVP.

I added a handful of new, 'Flavorful' abilities to "soften the blow".
My goal is to Make Azeroth FUN Again.
NOT obsess over numbers on a '40 Man Raid DPS Meter Add-on.'

 **BASELINE CHANGES:**
Arcane Surge has been reworked into '"Overload":
> (enemy players should NOT be heavily punished merely for having Resistances -- as they wisely should)

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/lciDbtL.png)

Polymorph cast time increased from 1.5 sec to 3 sec.
Blink CD increased from 15 --> 20 sec.
Remove Lesser Curse range has been reduced to 20 yards.
Early ranks of 'Frost Bolt' now have a 2.5 second cast time.

>>[**LINK TO NEW TALENT TREES**](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t0=aEakFcXgRS&t1=sEZF3OGjUa&t2=marVRCbsES)<<

 **ARCANE TREE IMPORTANT NOTES:**
 - 'Arcane Rupture' was problematic (infamous for 1 shotting in PVP) and is simply incompatible with my (and OG Blizz Devs) vision/philosophy for this Specialization.

 **NEW ABILITY:** 'Invisibility' from the beta of WoW! Its basically a free Invis Potion every 10 min. Tho in true 'goofball Magician' fashion its rather unreliable!

 **NEW ABILITY:** Quick-cast variant (Rabbit) of Polymorph which is intended for PVP usage (or escaping a mob).

 - Largely restored Arcane's original intended identity & character.
 - Returned (reworked) various iconic Vanilla Talents.
 - Reduced bonus damage to 75% as this tree was intended by OG devs not to dominate in raid DPS but to provide Sustainability/utility/survivability/amusing Magic Trick Gimmicks -- mostly in PVP.
 - "Arcane" was supposed to be a "Jack of All Trades" generic Magician so Fire/Frost are also slightly boosted in a few ways.

 **FIRE TREE IMPORTANT NOTES:**
No changes.  satisfied_turtle_head
Its the arch-typical 'glass cannon' spec and it seems reasonably balanced in my experience.

 **FROST TREE IMPORTANT NOTES:**
 - Icicles (infamous for cutting thru walls in PVP) has had its range reduced (and restricted) to 25 yards.
 - Reduced bonus damage to 75% as this tree was intended by OG devs not to dominate in raid DPS but to provide incredible AOE/control/survivability.
 - Slightly nerfed Ice Block (my Warrior changes would provide a direct counter to it).
 - Slightly nerfed Cold Snap as it ruins Arena PVP (requires investment to go back to 10 min CD)
 - Ice Barrier was buffed for survivability but "nerfed" for boosting damage (costs a point).

> **NOTE: If you want to see a more 'conservative/Raid-approved' version of Arcane --** [**CLICK HERE**](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=22267).

Blizz had deeply admirable concepts in regards to thematics and 'flavor' for Mage and its Trees -- these being very important in a fantasy Role Playing game.

>>LINK TO NEW TALENT TREES<<

- 'Arcane Rupture' was problematic (infamous for 1 shotting in PVP) and is simply incompatible with my (and OG Blizz Devs) vision/philosophy for this Specialization.
NEW ABILITY: 'Invisibility' from the beta of WoW! Its basically a free Invis Potion every 10 min. Tho in true 'goofball Magician' fashion its rather unreliable!

No changes.

subject: Re: Revamped Mage Talent Trees (UPDATED)
content_md:
This entire post is hard to take seriously.

It literally reads like it comes form someone who *only* plays PvP and has little to no idea as to why certain things are chosen the way they are. Not to mention that they speak of "Class Identity", when the Devs in Vanilla WoW had barely enough time to create any such thing in Vanilla times, all while entirely ignoring how several of their supposed "ideas from the devs" have actively not been made by them; things such as the Critical Damage in Frost being increased by 100%, not 50%; Blink being a staple in the class just like Polymorph; and many other things as well, which OP seemingly tries to make unusable.

Your Goal is to make Azeroth fun again? Stop killing a class. That would be an ideal start, seeing as you are so hellbent on it it seems. Fun versus Anti-Fun. And Fun wins out by a huge margin.

Also, hey, know how Overpower literally lets you bypass any form of Block and Parry, can crit for over 2k damage, all while entirely fine to have? Yeah, Mages are very much allowed to have something that bypasses Arcane resistance. Something, mind you, most PvP players tend to have because Polymorph exists.

Don't try to speak for the Original Devs. You don't seem to have an idea on what you are talking about in that aspect, considering you keep saying stuff like "Oh, Frost shouldn't deal damage". It doesn't do damage. It literally doesn't need a nerf because it *doesn't do damage*. It never did, not in Vanilla, not in Classic, not during fricking Season of Discovery where it was arguably the strongest, and not in Turtle WoW. If you really have that much trouble in PvP against mages, LEARN HOW TO PLAY AGAINST THEM. They *literally* explode if you look at them the wrong way if you know what you're doing.

author: Eluaria
subject: Flash Freeze: The issue with Inconsistency
content_md:
Inconsistency has never been a good part of the game, Vanilla Time or not. I know a lot of people love to disagree with this statement, but they are usually stuck upon things like "No changes are better" and the like, despite it being quite obvious that it's not really holding much validity in that regard.

In the Mage Class, there is notably just 1 thing that really impacts it for PVE fight, being Frostbite. A 15% chance to trigger a freeze effect may not sound like a huge deal, but when Turtle WoW attempted to change up the way Frost plays (mainly to being forced to be a 1-Button Wonder), they essentially attempted to fix it via a mechanic that doesn't really implement well into the game. While getting a Guaranteed proc via Frost Nova is rather fun, in practice there is a decent chance that a fight goes over without a single Flash Freeze Proc happening during it. The issue stems from the chance to freeze being static in vanilla, whereas in modern games (including WoW) there are failsafes in place to not be entirely dependent on RNG.

While Vanilla technically doesn't have that massive of an issue, with other classes using their Procs more as a buff to damage, Frost Mages rely on those procs to do the majority of their damage rotation.

Since people apparently are keen on complaining about Mages in PvP - a fact that is quite funny to me, considering how incredibly easy they are to kill, especially for Feral Druids or Rogues - I would like to make a suggestion that doesn't impact PvP related performance positively, while ultimately helping out the issue of Flash Freeze Procs being entirely dependent on a 15% chance.

![Image](https://cdn.imgchest.com/files/fbfee755d4dc.png)

Instead of having to fish for a Freeze Proc during the entirety of a fight, this now enables you to have a form of guarantee during a lengthy fight to throw out Flash Freeze enhanced Icicles every now and then. It also makes it so that PvP people cannot complain about it making it stronger outside of PvE fights. Because, frankly, it doesn't actually do anything in PvP.

author: Cheruscan
subject: Mage suggestions
content_md:
Playing a mage is very boring atm because arcane covers pretty much every aspect of the game for your class.

During lvling you best go arcane (low downtime, 0% spellpushback, highest hit chance from talents, etc)

During raiding you best go arcane (almost no arcane immune enemies, highest hit chance from talents, high dmg, easy to grasp rotation that is still a little engaging but never feels like chore)

During PvP you go arcane (high dps, channeled spell to ignore LOS, 0% pushback, instant cast pyroblast)

Fire specc is dead, it relies on multiple mages playing the specc in coordination, I know 2 mage mains and they both would love to play fire but they simply cant since mages are pretty rare and if there are other mages they are 95% arcane because its the most convenient specc

Frost specc is a meme you lose 15% of your dmg when you get hit... icicles feels like a worse arcane missile.

Pls turn arcane back into a support / gimmick specc make it have synergy with frost/fire again rather than being a standalone arcane dmg specc

Fire needs to be made more accesible, either rework ignite so a single fire mage can reliably keep it up or change the way the specc is supposed to do dmg, add more synergy with frost so a frost/fire specc can become a thing, hotstreak could count any spell crits no matter from which school, remove blastwave or give fire mages a real AoE playstyle using blastwave/flamestrike

In the lore fire magic is described as chaotic and volatile the capstone of fire should reflect this, maybe have the mage take dmg from his own firespells for a duration but buff your fire dmg at the same time.

Frost magic on the other hand is the prefered "safe and reliable" option for mages, the slows and shields are great but it lacks dmg. In PvE they could be given a stacking debuff on their target, smth like, stacks 6 times than explodes with frost dmg or just a dot akin to ignite but it doesnt need crits and it only works on enemies that are immune to the slow effects. Synergy with fire spells would also be great after 4 stacks the target loses fire immunity and will take 150% extra dmg from your next fire spell.

Arcane should offer talents for mana efficency and extra effects on all your spells in the first 4 rows, other people suggested giving poly and blink longer CDs and then have talents in deep arcane to bring them back to vanilla CD, for blink to problem, for poly it depends since its still a much needed tool, especially in dungeons. Deep arcane could still offer some arcane dmg, maybe add a chance to "empower" your next spell after hitting with arcane missiles, the empowered effect could be a debuff on the target or just simply "more" dmg but it should have different effects for different spells, easiest would be to "empower" by spell school ofc.

For example: your next fire dmg spell melts the targets armor increasing physical dmg taken by 10% for 5 seconds / your next frost dmg spell chills the target to its core reduces attack/cast speed by 40% for 4 seconds / your next arcane dmg spell ruptures the target dealing 200% extra dmg and increases arcane dmg taken by 8% for 12 seconds

Have all these on a seperate 15 sec internal cd so you cant procc the same effect over and over

author: Soulitics
subject: Addressing the Mage AOE nerf in PVE
content_md:
tl;dr- Why does PVE AOE Frost mage have to die? Why is the patch killing it not just for PVP?

First time making a post on here, have loved playing on Turtle wow and have enjoyed the community.
I have quit turtle wow ever since the major changes to Frost mage.
The changes are as follows:
Improved Blizzard: Slow amount reduced from 30/50/65% to 20/30/40%.

My biggest gripe with this is there is a developer note further down the patch changes that state: (talking about the ability they added New Talent: Icicles)
"We’ve opted to give this new part of the Frost Mage rotation a downside and the inability to slow your targets as we want to avoid giving even more power to Frost Mages in Player vs Player scenarios as they’re already a strong contender in that field while giving another tool to your rotation for Player vs Enemy scenarios where these downsides are much less likely to matter."

My only real issue is the crippling nerf to Blizzard aoe seems to be a PVP reason.
I'm confused as to why they would create a patch that makes Aoe farming impossible.
YES, you can kite with Cone of Cold. But even with that you're going to do way more often. You basically can't play frost aoe farming on Turtle.
I chatted with community members on the subject and heard lots of things of you should just deal with it, people saying I should play official, but no one wants to talk about why it even happened. I haven't talked to someone that actually plays frost mage and my biggest question is;

Is taking away a play-stye worth whatever harm Aoe frost is doing in PVE?

Because I cant be the only one that enjoyed AOE frost. I love playing hardcore, and I just have logged onto my character every month or so to see if i get to play the game the way I want to. Sure im biased to this specific play style and there are plenty of others. But why not just make it affected in PVP, is it a technical issue where it has to be for both PVP and PVE?

I have gotten 2 60 Frost mages on official
My mage on here sits at 46, I'd just like to play my favorite play-style on here.

There is a bit of a chain of events here that has to be considered. In Blizzards re-releaseclassic thanks to blizzards servers and players clients being way more powerful than back in 2004 it turned out mages could farm gold and exp so much more efficiently thanany other class that in order to parttake in any endgame gear you were basically requiredto have a mage or parttake in moneylau.... The blizzard nerf aimed to bring mage a bit closer to the pack in terms of its farming ability. Even with the nerfed blizzard, it is still possible to farm large packs thanks to frostnova and cone of cold. Its just a  bit less forgiving.

But then CC2 and its little cousin vampirism screwed over the economy balance once again, now with hunter traps and force reactive being left unchecked.

The right course of action here is to nerf the thing that is problematic now, not to unnerf the thing that was problematic before

You should pick a class on the grounds that you like its gameplay not wether or not you can afford to actually play it.

Having mage paladin and hunter all being able to farm to such a ridiculous degree still leaves 6 classes out. Rather nerf the 2 that are a problem now that mage has been reigned in and give all 9 classes the opportunity to actually farm

author: Avalok
subject: Allow 'Magic Attunement' to Affect All Levels
content_md:
The Mage's "Magic Attunement" talent in the Arcane tree
should, I believe, affect targets above level 62.

This way, the spell buffs affected by this talent can be useful in Raids,
and not just in Dungeons, specifically against Raid Bosses themselves.

This causes the Mage's Amplify and Dampen Magic spell buffs
to affect NPC targets other than themselves and other players.

This way, Mages could have an alternative to what Warlocks
have which is their Curse of Shadow and Curse of Elements.

If there is some balancing need about this, then maybe reduce the
amount of effectiveness increased by the talent from 100% to 50%.

author: Eluaria
subject: Devs, why is Frost Left being in the Dust?
content_md:
I am rather confused about the dev's approach to the next patch. While Arcane doesn't require any help, Fire is getting a change that literally fixes their biggest issue at the moment, essentially elevating their ability to deal damage without having to force a cooldown out of their rotation.

What does Frost get?

A QoL change to Frost barrier's that moves 10% of the 15% Damage buff into a static buff. Which effectively helps on Bosses with constant AoE damage to grant 10% of its damage increase during them.

This change does actively nothing for the issue Frost currently has. It has nowhere close to the Burst Damage of the other two specs, it doesn't have the consistent damage of either spec either, nor does it have the consistent uptime to its damage windows like Arcane does.

I have to wonder why the Devs are actively deciding not to up the Spell Power Ratios on Frostbolt and Icicles, and to change the way that icicles triggers, if not entirely rework the Spell and Mechanic into something more usable than it is now. I want to play Frost, but choosing to do so will *actively* harm my raid team by how much of a damage difference it makes past MC.

author: Eluaria
subject: Re: Devs, why is Frost Left being in the Dust?
content_md:
There are several things mentioned in the replies I want to answer to.

> Is subtlety rogue good, or beast master hunter? you have two good specs, just use one of them instead of frost

This is an absolute nil argument.

Just because other classes have the same problem does not make it a good point to throw out. If anything, this just means that Beastmaster and Subtlety Rogue need changes too.

Not to mention, Subtlety is amazing as a support class and adds a bunch of damage to a raid that outvalues a singular rogue's own, people just don't play it because they want to be the ones doing the big numbers. And Beast master is LITERALLY being buffed in multiple ways, both baseline and talentwise, in the coming patch.

Going "Oh, just play something else" is redundant and doesn't further anything in any form.

> I dont get it? Its still best control based spec there is for mage?

The spec isn't. The only control you get from it are slightly stronger slows and an ability to get a Slow on your Blizzard while Reducing Frost Nova's cooldown. And a 15% chance to freeze on slow effects, which only really applies to Improved Blizzard which you need to also Spec into, or a bare chance on Cone of Cold/Frostbolt, which is essentially gambling to have any effect.

Most of these are ADDITIONS to the control which Mage already has baseline. Cone of Cold, Frost Bolt, Polymorph, Frost Nova all exist baseline. They aren't what makes the Spec, they are just a baseline to the class.

This doesn't change anything about Frost having little identity in its own outside of "Slow, maybe sometimes freeze" and lacking both consistency and damage on top of that.

> I could be wrong but I think the devs want frost to be more of a pvp spec.

I'm not likely to be in the minority when I say that PvP is not and should not be the balance focus of a game that is 75%+ PvE. If they want Frost to be PvP spec, they can add Talents to it that make it better for PvP that don't help in PvE and vice versa. WoW has always done that, and balancing these two things differently, giving damage in PvE where it is missing while reducing it in PvP, shouldn't just be a suggestion but is by far the easiest way to handle it.

As it stands, Frost is okay in Arena PvP, but doesn't really hold up in BGs, considering Arcane and Fire just outburst and outsustain it by a lot. Frost's only saving grace is the utility it provides in PvP, and even then it is notably better to just kill someone quickly rather than trying to outsurvive them slowly.

If the devs really want Frost to be a PvP spec, they have not done a good job so far.

> My guess is that devs havent decided on mage specc directions yet, they fleshed out arcane but essentially made it a mono specc with no connection to fire or frost

I like this as an idea, however I fear it's not as simple, considering how Fire is very much holding up in Kara40 and is getting the QoL change it needs to fix their current issue with Fireblast dropping Ignite. The Turtle Discord even got one of the devs to answer to that specifically, but regarding Frost it has been dead silence for a while now.

> Fire mage does not see much play outside of coordinated mage teams rn since a solo fire mage will only serve as a fire shaman/fire lock buffer.

This is, factually, wrong. Some of the best Mages on the Nordanaar Server are playing Fire, and they aren't just keeping up with Arcane, they can outdamage them. The issue Fire has is its dependency on Crits, which you can not fully rely on, which is the main reason Arcane is played over it. Consistency in Classic is extremely powerful and Arcane just has those tools which Fire lacks. However, this does not mean that the spec is dead or doesn't see play outside of coordinated teams.

As such, you are not correct in assuming that Fire is dependent on other Fire Mages. Most Mage Players simply don't fully grasp that currently Fire Blast isn't part of the rotation unless you have a fully stacked Pyroblast ready, and that they need specific items to fully keep up with Arcane's consistency.

As it stands, Arcane is the best spec due to that aforementioned consistent gameplay loop, but Fire is entirely capable of being competitive and is preferred by multiple mages both on the discord and those not on it. The data for the fight turnouts show the same, where Fire Mages that do show up very much keep up in the damage ranges Arcane has, they are just heavily outnumbered.

This doesn't make Frost's place any better, and Frost doesn't need buffs in PvP and especially not follow-up backwards buffs with a "When Immune" mechanic that is so inconsistent as is that you can have entire fights without a single Proc coming from Frostbolt due to it being a static chance and the way chances are calculated in Vanilla. Frost needs either an overhaul or buffs in general, because while it may be the most used PvP spec, if you look at the Arcane and Fire mages who just make use of the Base Line abilities shared with Frost, you notice very quickly that these specs are favored in PvP as well.

author: Eluaria
subject: Re: Started playing frost mage and have questions
content_md:
I cannot recommend playing Frost in Raids. Even Fire (with a Spell Penetration build) outdoes it in Molten Core and Arcane is simply miles above it. With BWL now up and running, Frost will be left in the dust, sadly.

Until the Devs actually rework and Buff Frostmage, it will not be playable outside of Open World Content.

It DOES excel there. The survivability is absurdly good to the point you can solo many Elite Quests that almost all classes have issues doing. However, generally speaking, it is likely better to run a Fire Build with a decent amount of Points in Frost for survivability, as it will be faster kills overall.

Also, Darkhann understates the nerf to Blizzard. We lost a ton of damage on it, while also losing Damage on Improved Cone of Cold and a Reduction of Improved Blizzard's Slow. It is better to utilize Flamestrike, Frost Nova, and Cone of Cold to kite and AoE farm, with some Arcane Explosions inbetween. For AoE farming, we don't use Blizzard at all anymore, the nerfs are simply way too hard.

author: Chev03
subject: Re: 1.18 Leveling specs
content_md:
Hey most folks go Frost but Fire got a lot of love on Turtle WoW

In leveling you can go for any spec you want really. I would always go for sustain (e.g. reduce mana of spell x) or reduce cast time (like Fireball) or survivability talents (change to stun from fire spells)

I am leveling a Fire Mage currently and its kinda fun. I would generally advice to keep your gear up 2 date for your level (get the recent dungeon, quest or profession items) as this will have the biggest impact on your leveling experience. Frost is a bit less gear dependent if I remember correctly. What matters is to have resources like mana up and reduce downtime to regenerate.

You can also choose to go Alchemy and Herbalism to always have mana pots and elixirs. Standard is Tailoring Enchanting.

Have fun with your mage :)

author: Eluaria
subject: Re: 1.18 Leveling specs
content_md: Generally speaking, Frost wins out as an Open World Levelling Spec. The ability to freeze enemies in place and kite is incredibly useful and enables the spec to actually solo elite quests, which the other 2 specs can't reliably do. You can technically run full fire and use frostbolt, Frost Nova, and Cone of Cold without any enhancements to kite, but it is definitely harder. Arcane I can only recommend for Dungeons, Open World it is by far weaker than the other 2, although it will win out against Frost in late game content.
